name: Meta FAIR Chemistry: Open Catalyst, OMat24, OMol25 and UMA
subcategory: open DFT datasets and universal interatomic potentials (catalysis, materials, molecules, MOFs)
origin_detail: Meta Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) Chemistry team; the Open Catalyst Project was 'a collaborative research effort' of FAIR and Carnegie Mellon University's Department of Chemical Engineering. OMol25 electronic-structure data are hosted at Argonne National Laboratory via Globus.

licences.weights: custom: OMat24 License (2024-10-23) and FAIR Chemistry License v1 (2025-05-14; commercial use allowed, acceptable-use policy, gated)
licences.data: CC BY 4.0 (OMat24, OMol25; OMol25 repo gated and geo-restricted)

openness_notes: Code MIT. Datasets: OC20 (1,281,040 DFT relaxations, about 264.89M single points) and baselines 'provided as open resources' (2020; dataset licence not stated on fetched pages); OMat24 CC BY 4.0 (100.8M training structures plus 10.4M sAlex); OMol25 CC BY 4.0 (over 100M DFT calculations at wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD, about 83M unique systems, 'billions of CPU core-hours'). Checkpoints moved to custom licences. The OMat24 eqV2/eSEN checkpoints use the 'OMat24 License' (2024-10-23, FAIR Acceptable Use Policy, gated). UMA uses the 'FAIR Chemistry License v1' (2025-05-14), which allows 'commercial and non-commercial use' but adds an acceptable-use policy (no military, weapons or critical-infrastructure uses), indemnity and gating (legal name, date of birth, organisation). The OMol25 HF repo is unavailable in 'comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, and in China, Russia, and Belarus'. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Initial 3 (open data, code and baselines); current 2 (fully open data and code; custom, gated weights).

license_history.license: MIT code; OC20 data and baselines 'open resources' (data licence not confirmed)
OMat24 dataset CC BY 4.0; OMat24 checkpoints under custom 'OMat24 License' (gated)
OMol25 dataset CC BY 4.0 (gated, geo-restricted); UMA under FAIR Chemistry License v1 (gated)

relicensing_events.from: MIT-licensed code and openly provided baselines (OC20 era)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Applies to weights only; the datasets stayed CC BY 4.0. OC20-era checkpoint licences were not confirmed.

relicensing_events.to: FAIR Chemistry License v1 (commercial use allowed, acceptable-use policy, gated; OMol25 repo blocked in China, Russia, Belarus)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Permissive on commercial use but not an OSI licence: the Llama-style pattern applied to chemistry. Third parties retrained OSI-licensed models on the CC BY data (Orb, MACE, SevenNet).

risk_events: Custom licence and gating on weights; geographic restrictions
Open Catalyst Project described in the past tense ('was a collaborative research effort')
robustness: CC BY 4.0 datasets let others train independent models (Orb, MACE, SevenNet were trained on OMat24/OMol25), so the ecosystem does not depend on Meta's checkpoints.
physical_science_relevance: Catalysis, inorganic materials, molecular chemistry and MOFs for carbon capture; OMol25 is among the largest open quantum-chemistry datasets, hosted with a DOE lab (Argonne).

training_data.name: OC20, OC22, ODAC23, OMat24, OMol25, OMC25
training_data.access: open (CC BY 4.0 confirmed for OMat24 and OMol25)
training_data.note: UMA is trained on 'five open-science simulation datasets from the FAIR Chemistry team'.

training_data.name: MPtrj, sAlexandria
training_data.note: Used with OMat24 for the OAM checkpoints.

openness_effect_assessment: Meta's CC BY datasets became the shared training substrate of the field: OMat24 and OMol25 underpin Orb, MACE, SevenNet and UMA itself. Meta kept partial control by putting custom, gated licences on its own weights.
key_takeaway: Meta is the most generous corporate data publisher in materials and chemistry (hundreds of millions of DFT calculations, CC BY 4.0). It uses Llama-style custom licences for the models. Data openness, not weight openness, has had the larger spillover.
